description: Repeated Wind Tunnel Section Model Tests of a Closed-Box Bridge Deck – Scanlan Derivatives is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Luca Caracoglia, Northeastern University (northeastern.edu). Scanlan derivatives (i.e. flutter derivatives) are force coefficients employed for aeroelastic analysis of long-span bridges. These coefficients are usually determined through wind tunnel tests. The data set shared herein is related to the test results of a set of free decay aeroelastic experiments, carried out in the wind tunnel of Northeastern University, Boston, MA (USA). Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-6xp3-xj95. Keywords: Long-span bridges; aeroelasticity; Scanlan (flutter) derivatives; wind tunnel tests.. Published 2020-05-29. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
